component.name: TuxRGB
component.summary: Control the RGB lighting of your whole PC
Pilotez l'éclairage RGB de tout votre PC

description.p: TuxRGB synchronises the RGB lighting of your motherboard, RAM, graphics card, fans, AIO coolers, keyboards, mice and LED strips from a single, modern interface.

It ships the OpenRGB hardware engine (release 1.1, with the latest upstream device support), so every device supported by OpenRGB works without installing anything else. The interface is native Wayland, follows the Material 3 Expressive design language, speaks English and French, and takes its colours from your desktop accent (KDE Plasma, GNOME, COSMIC).

ul.li: Visual map: place, rotate and resize your devices so effects travel across your real desk
19 effects: static, breathing, rainbow and gradient waves, aurora, plasma, fire, comet, scanner, rain, bubbles, swirl, thunderstorm, GLSL shaders…
Harmonious System Palette: multi-colour effects built from your desktop accent
Audio visualiser on every device (PipeWire) and per-LED screen sync (ScreenCast portal)
Hardware monitor: CPU / GPU temperature and load, memory, in colour
Smooth crossfades, global brightness and 0–200 % saturation
Fan speed control: fixed speeds or temperature curves for motherboard fans, with safety rules
LEDs off at shutdown, at sleep and while the screen is off, exact state restored afterwards
Guided, reversible setup of hardware access (udev rules, I2C/SMBus) through Polkit, on every major distribution
Runs from the system tray with near-zero CPU usage

description.p: TuxRGB synchronise l'éclairage RGB de la carte mère, de la RAM, de la carte graphique, des ventilateurs, du watercooling, des claviers, souris et bandes LED, ainsi que la vitesse des ventilateurs. Le moteur OpenRGB 1.1 est intégré : rien d'autre à installer. Interface Wayland native, Material 3 Expressive, en français et en anglais, couleurs reprises de l'accent du bureau (KDE Plasma, GNOME, COSMIC).

description.p: Fan control, and LEDs that turn off with the screen.

ul.li: New Fans page: every fan plugged into the motherboard with its live speed, left to the motherboard, set to a fixed speed or driven by a curve that follows the CPU, the GPU or a motherboard sensor (draggable points, Silent, Balanced and Performance presets)
Safety: every driven fan at full speed at 90 °C, the motherboard takes a fan back if its temperature can no longer be read, original settings restored on exit
Linux: a small system service applies the fan settings from boot, set up once through Polkit
Graphics card fans stay with their own tools (LACT on Linux, AMD Adrenalin or the NVIDIA app on Windows)
Windows: ITE and Nuvoton motherboard controllers through PawnIO in administrator mode
The LEDs fade out when the screen goes to sleep and come back with it (KDE Plasma, GNOME, other Wayland desktops after 10 minutes of inactivity, Windows)

description.p: The LEDs show the same colours as the app.

ul.li: LED colour correction, on by default: the colours go through the screen's curve (gamma) and a white balance before reaching the hardware, so a pink stays pink instead of turning purple and pastels are no longer washed out
Settings, LED colours: gamma, red, green and blue weights, and a white test to set a neutral white
The brightness slider keeps its feel

description.p: Windows: GPU load and temperature of any graphics card, CPU temperature and power without extra software.

ul.li: GPU load from the GPU engine counters and GPU temperature from the graphics kernel, as in the Task Manager: AMD, NVIDIA and Intel cards
CPU temperature and package power of AMD Ryzen and Intel Core processors through the signed PawnIO driver, in administrator mode

description.p: Windows installer without any script, so that Windows Defender no longer flags it.

ul.li: The installer no longer starts a PowerShell script to download OpenRGB and PawnIO: TuxRGB fetches OpenRGB itself over HTTPS and the signed PawnIO setup is carried in the installer

description.p: Global or per component effects, free rotation on the canvas and a new Displays page.

ul.li: The Effects page sets the effect of the whole setup; every device, zone or fan can follow it, play an effect of its own with its own settings, keep a colour or stay off
Canvas items turn to any angle: rotation slider and a rotation knob on the canvas, right angles magnetic

Displays page: NZXT Kraken Z / 2023 / 2024 and Corsair LCD screens, DeepCool digital displays, showing CPU / GPU temperature, load, power and clock, memory, the time, a text or a picture, at the refresh rate chosen, with a live preview
Open protocols re-implemented from liquidctl, deepcool-digital-linux and OpenLinkHub, over USB HID, without the vendor software
More sensors: CPU and GPU power and clock, memory in GiB; on Windows, CPU temperature and AMD / Intel graphics sensors read from LibreHardwareMonitor while it runs

description.p: Per fan per header, network lights, hardware effects and a new saturation.

ul.li: An ARGB header can be split into fans, like OpenRGB segments, each with its own LED count: every fan is an item of the canvas, placed, turned and resized on its own, and follows the effect, keeps its colour or stays off
Canvas items can be hidden while staying connected and lit; the selected item comes to the front; orientation 0°, 90°, 180° or 270°
Keyboards, mice and WiZ bulbs can play their own built-in effect instead of TuxRGB's
WLED controllers (DDP, LED count detected) and Philips WiZ bulbs (network search) become devices like any other
Perceptual saturation (Okhsv): no hue drift, no clipping, brightness unchanged, applied to the hardware on the next frame
Every LED, motherboard and fans included, is turned off at shutdown, logout and sleep within a strict 400 ms limit: the system is never slowed down

description.p: Fixes a device that sometimes stayed lit at shutdown or sleep.

ul.li: After turning the LEDs off for a shutdown or sleep, a frame rendered just before could reach a device afterwards and light it again (often the motherboard and its ARGB fans): the LEDs now stay dark until the resume
Black is written a second time and confirmed, so slow controllers are really dark before the system goes down

description.p: Fixes LEDs that only changed every few seconds on PCs with slow controllers.

ul.li: Colours go through a connection of their own: each device is updated at its own pace, so RGB memory (SMBus) or a graphics card (I2C) that takes hundreds of milliseconds per write no longer holds back the mouse, keyboard, fans or motherboard
A slow acknowledgement is no longer taken for a lost connection (which made the lighting freeze for several seconds while TuxRGB reconnected)
Turning the LEDs off (quit, shutdown, sleep) writes every device at once and waits for slow ones

description.p: Released for Linux and Windows at the same time, with the same fixes.

ul.li: Built-in updates: Settings → Updates checks the GitHub releases, downloads the AppImage, verifies its SHA-256 and restarts TuxRGB
Optional automatic check at start-up, at most every 6 hours
Global saturation above 100 % now also deepens colours that are already pure (rainbow, primary colours, accent colours)

description.p: Embedded hardware engine updated to OpenRGB 1.1. The interface is unchanged.

ul.li: Fixes a deadlock with ENE SMBus RAM and motherboard lighting (ASUS Aura DRAM and many RGB memory modules)
Mode changes and LED colours sent right after them are always applied in order
Hot-plug fixes in several controllers; Sinowealth mice no longer crash or lose their configuration
Cooler Master ARGB Gen2 A1 V2 fixed; MSI GeForce RTX 3070 Gaming Trio Plus and Kreo Swarm (wired) supported

description.p: Performance and reliability. The interface is unchanged.

ul.li: Minimised window: the live preview slows down to a few frames per second as soon as the window is no longer drawn (about 2 % CPU instead of a full core with software rendering)
In the tray with only demo devices, the effect engine sleeps completely; the memory of a closed window is given back to the system
The soft glow behind the previews is built off the interface thread; frames, colour buffers, screen and shader captures reuse their memory instead of allocating every frame

OpenRGB: hot-plugged devices and zones resized elsewhere are noticed from the server's notifications; the device list is watched with a cheap request instead of reading every controller every ten seconds
Hot-plug safety: a frame built for an old layout of a device is never written to it; the selected device stays selected when another one appears or disappears
Settings are written in the background, flushed to disk, and read once at start-up; a crash or power cut can no longer leave an empty configuration
Tray icon registered even when TuxRGB starts before the panel at login
Time limits on the desktop portal, notifications, nvidia-smi and the kernel log; a sleeping laptop GPU is no longer woken up by the hardware monitor
Shader effect recovers from a GPU read-back failure; a crashed capture thread can no longer freeze the reactive effects
Larger, clearer live preview on the effects page, with device names
Hardware monitor, automatic sensor: devices without a sensor of their own (keyboard, mouse, mat, headset…) follow the CPU temperature, or the CPU load when it cannot be read
New setting: speed of the app animations (25 to 300 %)

description.p: Finishing touches.

ul.li: New application icon (window, menu, tray)
Smooth transitions everywhere: page and wizard fade-through, dialogs, colour picker, banners, panels, selections, text fields, scrollbars and wheel scrolling
Immersive previews: the whole canvas glows with a soft, blurred rendering of the effect behind the devices
Brightness and saturation follow the sliders almost instantly; tray updates are coalesced
Single-colour SMBus devices always receive the final colour of a slider

description.p: Full release.

ul.li: New native effects from the OpenRGB plugins: plasma, fire, comet, scanner, rain, bubbles, swirl, thunderstorm, GLSL shaders (GPU) and hardware monitor (CPU/GPU/RAM)
Visual map: rotation, mirroring, resize handle; screen sync samples exactly the area each LED covers
Audio visualiser reaches every device ("spectrum on every device"), lower latency
Harmonious System Palette for multi-colour effects; desktop accent from KDE, GNOME or COSMIC
Crossfades between colours, effects, presets and accent changes; saturation up to 200 %
Expressive sliders (thickening track, squash and stretch handle, value bubble), squishy buttons
English and French interface, system language detected
SMBus fix on every distribution (rpm-ostree, grubby, kernelstub, GRUB, systemd-boot, rEFInd), only when needed
LEDs turned off at shutdown, logout and sleep; restored at start
Tray icon listed with applications; problem banners and desktop notifications with direct actions

description.p: Hardened hardware access (uaccess only, no world-writable udev rules, strictly validated privileged helper), Saturation slider for single-colour effects, Material 3 Expressive refresh with animated buttons and switches, maximised window from the menu and tray-only start at login.

One-click configuration of empty ARGB headers, Static and Breathing can follow the KDE Plasma accent colour, every setting saved in config.json and restored at login, single instance (a new launch brings the window forward), maximised window, smoother page transitions, no more duplicate udev rules on distributions that ship OpenRGB's, one-click SMBus fix for RAM lighting.

Latest OpenRGB device support (master, October 2026), addressable ARGB headers can be sized from the Devices page, devices without a Direct mode are driven through their Custom or Static mode, software brightness with a perceptual curve, instant password dialog, hardware report for RAM issues.
First release: embedded OpenRGB 1.0 engine, Material 3 Expressive interface, KDE accent colours, audio visualiser, screen sync, Polkit hardware setup wizard.
